title: Residual re-specialization around merged experts
hypothesis: After routing-guided cluster merging, compact shared residual Views recover member expert functions at lower complete bytes than independent experts; private residual budget marks where shared state stops sufficing.
mirror_coordinate: per-expert low-rank residual coordinates over a shared residual basis
logical_multiplicity: sixteen logical experts recovered from four merged experts

development.selection_metric: heldout expert-output nRMSE, complete serialized bytes, reconstruction and inference MAC

fresh.reason: shared-basis and private residual forms are compared to their exact native low-rank controls; no task audit after alias

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes

success_gate: At least one low private-rank condition has heldout nRMSE <=0.02 and >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent weights, with no more compute than independent inference and a Mirror-specific gain over native low-rank decompression.
failure_gate: FAIL for Mirror-specific value if native factorization exactly matches the representation, storage/quality gates fail, or private state eliminates savings.
boundaries: Synthetic linear expert banks and known routing clusters only; no trained M-SMoE/MC-SMoE, router statistics, or language model claim.
Oracle checkpoints are generated from a shared low-rank residual plus private Gaussian heterogeneity.
Matrix reconstruction is a one-time load operation; inference MAC and reconstruction MAC are reported separately.
